title: Latency/$ Benchmark Report — Chart Specification (web + PDF)
content:
Doc purpose
Define the exact charts to generate for the public-facing Latency/$ benchmark report (landing page + PDF). This is the single source of truth for:
- which plots we publish
- axes + units
- how to map raw benchmark fields to plotted values
- color + style rules (Redwood visual system)
- QA checks to avoid misleading visualizations

Audience
- Design (layout + styling), Marketing (narrative ordering), Applied ML/Evals (metric correctness), Web/DX (implementation).


Data inputs (authoritative)
Primary dataset (internal):
- Drive: shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmark-results-raw-table.json
- One row per (run_id, model_id, region, workload, config_id)

Public-facing table export (sanitized):
- Generated by benchmark-lab export pipeline (see PR-159)
- Contains aggregated stats per (model_id, region, workload, config_id)

Required raw fields (minimum)
(Exact field names may differ slightly in the export; if so, add a mapping layer but keep semantics identical.)
- model_id (string) e.g., "llama-3.1-70b-instruct", "qwen2.5-72b-instruct"
- model_family (string) e.g., "Llama", "Qwen", "Mistral" (used for grouping)
- model_size_b (number-as-string ok) e.g., "70", "72"
- region (string) e.g., "us-east", "us-west", "eu-central", "ap-southeast"
- provider (string) always "Redwood" for this report version
- workload (string) one of: "chat", "embeddings"
- concurrency (int)
- input_tokens_p50 (int) and output_tokens_p50 (int) OR total_tokens_p50 (int)
- latency_ms_p50, latency_ms_p95 (numbers)
- throughput_tok_s_mean (number) (output token/s; if only total token/s exists, document and consistently use)
- cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens (number)
- cost_usd_per_request_p50 (number) (preferred) OR enough data to compute it deterministically
- variance_latency_ms_p50_cv (number) OR similar variance measure to decide when to show error bars
- sample_size_requests (int)
- run_window_start, run_window_end (timestamps) (for footnotes / versioning)


Derived metrics (for plotting)
1) Cost per request (p50)
- If cost_usd_per_request_p50 exists: use directly.
- Else compute using token counts from the workload definition and the effective price:
  cost_usd_per_request_p50 = (input_tokens_p50 + output_tokens_p50) * price_usd_per_token_effective
  where price_usd_per_token_effective = cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens / 1,000,000 for output tokens only.
  NOTE: Only do this fallback if methodology explicitly says cost is output-token based. Otherwise require cost_usd_per_request_p50.

2) Latency/$ score (our headline “production economics” metric)
We need a single monotonic score where higher = better. Use the exported “latency_per_dollar” if provided by benchmark-lab. If we must compute:
- Define perf_per_dollar = (1 / latency_ms_p50) / cost_usd_per_request_p50
- Then scale for readability:
  latency_per_dollar_score = perf_per_dollar * 1,000
Units: (1/ms)/$ * 1,000. This is a score, not a physical unit; label as “Latency/$ score (higher is better)”.

3) Throughput/$ (secondary)
If needed for a supporting chart:
- throughput_per_dollar = throughput_tok_s_mean / cost_usd_per_second
- cost_usd_per_second = (throughput_tok_s_mean * price_usd_per_token_effective)
=> throughput_per_dollar simplifies to 1 / price_usd_per_token_effective if throughput_tok_s_mean refers to output tokens and price applies to output tokens. This can become misleading.
Therefore: Only use throughput/$ if methodology supports it and cost model is aligned. Prefer “cost per 1M tokens” + “latency p50/p95” as separate charts.


Chart inventory (public)
We will ship these charts in both Web (interactive/responsive) and PDF (static). The web version may include hover tooltips and filters; the PDF should show a single “default view” with a note that more slices are available on the landing page.

CH-0. Hero: Latency/$ leaderboard (topline)
Purpose: One glance “who wins on production economics” per region.
Type: grouped horizontal bar chart (recommended) OR dot plot.
Filters (web): workload=chat (default), region selector.
Data granularity: one point per model_id within the region.
X axis: latency_per_dollar_score (higher better). Unit label: “Latency/$ score (↑ better)”.
Y axis: model_id (display name; see naming rules).
Sorting: descending by latency_per_dollar_score.
Color: by model_family (see Color Rules).
Annotations:
- Show p50 latency and cost per 1M tokens in tooltip (web) / footnote table (PDF small).
- Show sample_size_requests in tooltip.

CH-1. Latency vs Cost scatter (engineer-friendly tradeoff view)
Purpose: Show the frontier; avoid implying one number tells the whole story.
Type: scatter plot with optional label for top performers.
One chart per region (PDF shows 2–3 regions; web has region tabs).
X axis: cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens (USD). Label: “Cost ($) per 1M output tokens”. Log scale: NO (keep linear for readability unless range > 10x; if log, must label clearly).
Y axis: latency_ms_p50. Label: “p50 latency (ms)”.
Point size: model_size_b (optional; if used, add legend and keep min/max sizes subtle).
Point color: model_family.
Callouts:
- Highlight 3–5 points that sit on the Pareto frontier per region.
- Add diagonal guidance text: “Upper-right = slower + more expensive”.

CH-2. Region comparison: Latency/$ by region for top models
Purpose: Make regional differences explicit without “cherry-picking” a best region.
Type: small multiples (recommended) OR grouped bars.
Default selection: top 6 models by global-average latency/$ (computed across regions with equal weight). Must document selection rule in caption.
X axis: region.
Y axis: latency_per_dollar_score.
Series: model_id.
Color: by model_id (NOT family) to keep series consistent across panels.
Legend: yes (PDF), hover labels (web).
Caption requirement: “Benchmarks run independently per region; differences can reflect hardware availability, network path, and fleet load controls.”

CH-3. Latency distribution summary (p50 + p95)
Purpose: Guardrail against optimizing for median only.
Type: dumbbell plot (preferred) OR paired bars.
Granularity: per model_id within a region (default region = us-east).
X axis: latency (ms).
Y axis: model_id.
Two marks per row: p50 and p95 with a connecting line.
Color: single neutral (graphite) for the line; p50 dot in Redwood blue; p95 dot in Redwood orange.
Tooltip: include sample_size_requests and variance metric.

CH-4. Cost breakdown / “what you pay for” (supporting)
Purpose: Procurement-friendly view; anchors dollars.
Type: table + bar (hybrid) OR bar chart only.
X axis: model_id.
Y axis: cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens.
Optional stacked segments (only if we have defensible split): input vs output cost. If we do not, do NOT imply split.
Color: single hue gradient by cost (lower cost lighter). Ensure accessible contrast.
Note: If input vs output not available, keep a simple bar chart with exact values on bars.

CH-5. Embeddings: cost vs throughput and latency
Purpose: Keep embeddings separate; avoid mixing apples/oranges.
Type: 2-panel chart (same page/section)
Panel A: cost_usd_per_1m_embeddings (if defined) OR cost_usd_per_1m_tokens for embeddings workload.
Panel B: latency_ms_p50 (embeddings).
X axis (both): model_id (embeddings model).
Y axis: cost / latency.
Color: by model_family.
Footnote: embeddings workload definition differs from chat (sequence lengths, batching).

CH-6. Variance / confidence visualization (only if we can defend)
Purpose: Credibility; show we measured stability.
Type: bar chart with error bars OR violin if we have per-run distributions.
Default: show CV (coefficient of variation) for latency_ms_p50 across repeated runs.
X axis: model_id.
Y axis: latency_ms_p50_cv (unitless). Label: “Run-to-run p50 latency CV (↓ better)”.
Color: neutral.
Inclusion rule: Only show if sample_size_requests >= threshold and number of repeated runs >= 3. If not, drop this chart and keep the variance language in text.


Non-goals / charts we explicitly will NOT publish (v1)
- Any chart that ranks “overall best model” without region + workload qualifiers.
- Any chart that mixes chat and embeddings in a single axis.
- Any chart using log scales without explicit labeling and rationale.
- Any chart that uses raw per-request logs or includes customer-identifying traces.


Naming + labeling rules
Model display names
- Use vendor canonical names but simplify suffixes where possible.
- Example: “Llama 3.1 70B Instruct” (display) from model_id=llama-3.1-70b-instruct.
- Keep “quantized” flags explicit if used (e.g., “(INT8)”). Never hide quantization.
- If two variants exist (context length, quant profile), add a footnote marker and show full config in tooltip.

Region display names
- Use marketing-friendly region labels consistent with docs: “US East”, “US West”, “EU Central”, “APAC Southeast”.
- If we need exact cloud region codes, include in tooltip or appendix table.

Units
- Latency always in milliseconds (ms).
- Cost always in USD, with “per 1M output tokens” explicitly stated.
- Throughput always “output tokens/s” unless explicitly total tokens/s; must match methodology.

Rounding
- latency_ms: round to nearest 1 ms for p50; nearest 5 ms for p95 if needed to reduce label noise.
- cost_usd_per_1m_output_tokens: show with 2 decimals if >= $1.00; else 3 decimals.
- latency_per_dollar_score: show with 1 decimal.


Color rules (Redwood visual system)
Primary palette (use exact hex)
- Redwood Blue: #2563EB (primary highlight)
- Redwood Teal: #0EA5A4
- Redwood Orange: #F97316
- Redwood Purple: #7C3AED
- Graphite (text/axes): #111827
- Slate (gridlines): #E5E7EB

Family mapping (consistent across all charts)
- Llama family: Blue (#2563EB)
- Qwen family: Teal (#0EA5A4)
- Mistral family: Purple (#7C3AED)
- “Other” / mixed: Graphite (#111827) with 40% opacity fill where appropriate
If additional families added, pick from the palette above first; do not introduce new colors without updating this doc.

Accessibility
- Minimum 4.5:1 contrast for text on backgrounds.
- Do not rely on color alone: add shape variations for scatter points if we have >3 families (circle/triangle/square) in web; in PDF, keep to <=4 categories.


Layout + sizing guidelines
Web
- Default chart container: 1200px width desktop, responsive down to 360px.
- Tooltips must include: model, region, workload, p50/p95, cost per 1M, sample size, run window.
- Provide filters: region, workload, model family, model size bucket (<=14B, 15–40B, 41–80B, >80B) if we have enough data.

PDF
- Page width: US Letter + A4 compatible (avoid micro text).
- Prefer small multiples over dense legends.
- Every figure must include a caption with: workload, region(s), measurement window (month/year), and a one-sentence disclaimer.


Mapping from raw metrics to visuals (implementation notes)
- All charts must use the same “selected slice” definition:
  - workload: chat unless chart is embeddings section
  - concurrency: use the report’s default concurrency (from methodology). Do not mix concurrency levels in one chart.
  - warmup/caching policy: implicit from benchmark run; do not annotate caching “wins” as product feature.

- Aggregation rule for public charts:
  - If multiple runs exist for the same (model, region, workload, config), use median of p50 latency and median of cost metrics.
  - p95 latency: use median of p95 across runs.
  - variance chart uses the distribution across runs.

- Outlier handling (public):
  - If the anomaly triage playbook marked a data point as excluded, it should not appear anywhere. Keep an internal appendix with the excluded list.


QA checklist (before publishing)
- [ ] Axes labels include units (ms, USD per 1M output tokens).
- [ ] No chart mixes chat + embeddings.
- [ ] Any ranking chart is explicitly scoped to a region + workload.
- [ ] Latency/$ score definition matches the computed/exported field exactly (verify with Applied ML).
- [ ] For every figure, confirm the underlying dataset version/date.
- [ ] Spot check 3 models across 2 regions: do the plotted numbers match the public table export?
- [ ] Tooltips/captions include “higher is better” vs “lower is better” consistently.
- [ ] Color mapping consistent across all charts.
- [ ] If any log scale used, add explicit label + rationale in caption.


Open questions (need decisions)
1) Do we include APAC in PDF v1, or keep APAC web-only with a callout? (Marketing + Field feedback)
2) Do we show absolute $ cost numbers in the hero leaderboard tooltip, or keep cost in separate chart only? (concern: people screenshot leaderboards without context)
3) Confirm whether cost is output-token only or total tokens for the default workload; this impacts cost per request computation and tooltips.

Change log
- 2025-02-04: Added CH-6 variance visualization inclusion rule.
- 2025-02-11: Updated family color mapping to match landing page visual system draft.
- 2025-02-17: Clarified Latency/$ score computation + labeling (“score, higher is better”).
